question: In datasets covering hundreds of thousands of teenagers, digital technology use explains at most what share of variation in well-being?
answer: About 0.4%. Orben and Przybylski analysed three large datasets and found the link between technology use and adolescent well-being was tiny, about the size of the link between eating potatoes and well-being in the same data. Small on average does not mean nothing for any one teenager.
move: Ask how big an effect is, not only whether one exists.
trap: Loud public worry makes a large share feel likely.
source: Orben and Przybylski, Nature Human Behaviour, 2019
reference: Orben and Przybylski, The association between adolescent well-being and digital technology use, Nature Human Behaviour, 2019
